exercises.instructions: Builds the lats, the back muscles behind a pull-up. Pull the bar or handles down to your upper chest by driving your elbows toward your ribs, then let them rise slowly. Anchor the band high overhead.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Builds the lats, the back muscles behind a pull-up. Pull the bar or handles down to your upper chest by driving your elbows toward your ribs, then let them rise slowly. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Builds the lats, the back muscles behind a pull-up. Pull the bar or handles down to your upper chest by driving your elbows toward your ribs, then let them rise slowly. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Lat Stretch
exercises.instructions: Hold a door frame or post overhead and sink your hips back and away to stretch the side of your back.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
exercises.instructions: With a band around your legs, bend your knees slightly and step sideways while keeping tension. Burns the side glutes.

exercises.name: Lateral Box Jump
exercises.instructions: Jump sideways onto a box from both feet, land softly, and step down.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
exercises.instructions: Step wide to one side and sit your hips back into that leg while the other leg stays straight, then push back to the start.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Step wide to one side and sit your hips back into that leg while the other leg stays straight, then push back to the start. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, or one at your chest.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Step wide to one side and sit your hips back into that leg while the other leg stays straight, then push back to the start. Hold the kettlebell at your chest, goblet-style.

exercises.name: Lateral Neck Flexion (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Lying on your side with a plate held against the side of your head, bring your ear toward your shoulder. Go slowly and keep it light.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Band)
exercises.instructions: Builds the side of the shoulders. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. The band gets harder as it stretches, so the end of each rep is the toughest.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Builds the side of the shoulders. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the side of the shoulders. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the side of the shoulders. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Builds the side of the shoulders. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows, then lower slowly. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Up
exercises.instructions: Step up sideways onto a box, driving through the leg on top, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: Leaning Lateral Raise (Cable)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm lateral raise while leaning away from a post or cable stack, which loads the start of the movement. The cable keeps tension on the shoulder from the very first inch.

exercises.name: Leaning Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm lateral raise while leaning away from a post or cable stack, which loads the start of the movement. Hold a sturdy post with your free hand and let your body lean out to the side.

exercises.name: Leg Curl (Band)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the hamstrings. Curl your heels toward your glutes against resistance, squeeze, and lower slowly. Anchor the band low and loop it around your ankle.

exercises.name: Leg Curl (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the hamstrings. Curl your heels toward your glutes against resistance, squeeze, and lower slowly. Strap an ankle cuff to the low pulley and curl standing or lying face down.

exercises.name: Leg Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the hamstrings. Curl your heels toward your glutes against resistance, squeeze, and lower slowly. Lie face down on a bench and hold the dumbbell between your feet.

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Band)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the quads. Straighten your legs against resistance until your knees lock, squeeze, and lower slowly. Anchor the band low behind you and loop it around your ankle.

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the quads. Straighten your legs against resistance until your knees lock, squeeze, and lower slowly. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Leg Press (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine press for the quads and glutes. Lower the platform until your knees reach about 90°, then press it away without locking your knees hard.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Calf raises on a leg press machine: push the platform with the balls of your feet and let your heels stretch back.

exercises.name: Leg Swings
exercises.instructions: Hold onto something and swing one leg forward and back (or side to side) in a relaxed arc. A good dynamic warm-up.

exercises.name: Legless Rope Climb
exercises.instructions: Climb a rope using only your arms, legs held still. Builds serious pulling strength and grip.

exercises.name: Lizard Pose
exercises.instructions: A deep lunge stretch with both hands inside your front foot, sinking your hips low to open the hips and groin.

exercises.name: Log Clean and Press
exercises.instructions: A strongman lift: roll the log up to your shoulders, then press it overhead.

exercises.name: Log Press
exercises.instructions: A strongman overhead press with a thick log held by its neutral handles, usually after cleaning it to your chest.

exercises.name: Low Row (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine row pulling from a low angle toward your lower ribs, working the lats and mid-back.

exercises.name: Low-Bar Squat (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A back squat with the bar lower on your shoulder blades and more forward lean, bringing the hips and posterior chain in more.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.instructions: A cable fly from low pulleys, bringing the handles up and together at shoulder height to target the upper chest.

exercises.name: Lu Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A lateral raise continued all the way overhead with thumbs up, named after weightlifter Lu Xiaojun. Great for shoulder strength and health; keep it light.

exercises.name: Lunge
exercises.instructions: A single-leg staple for the quads and glutes. Step forward and lower until both knees bend to about 90°, back knee just above the floor, then push back up to standing.

exercises.name: Lunge (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A single-leg staple for the quads and glutes. Step forward and lower until both knees bend to about 90°, back knee just above the floor, then push back up to standing. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Lunge (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A single-leg staple for the quads and glutes. Step forward and lower until both knees bend to about 90°, back knee just above the floor, then push back up to standing. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, which keeps the weight low and easy to balance.

exercises.name: Lunge (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A single-leg staple for the quads and glutes. Step forward and lower until both knees bend to about 90°, back knee just above the floor, then push back up to standing. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides, or one at your chest, goblet-style.

exercises.name: Lunge (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: A single-leg staple for the quads and glutes. Step forward and lower until both knees bend to about 90°, back knee just above the floor, then push back up to standing. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine leg curl lying face down: curl your heels toward your glutes, squeeze the hamstrings, and lower slowly.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back with hands under your hips, raise your straight legs to vertical, then lower them slowly without letting your lower back arch.

exercises.name: Man Maker (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A brutal dumbbell complex: a push-up, a row with each arm, jump your feet in, clean the dumbbells and press them overhead.

exercises.name: Massage Gun
exercises.instructions: Percussive massage for recovery: glide the gun slowly over tight muscles for a minute or two each. Avoid bones and joints.

exercises.name: Meadows Row (Landmine)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm row on the end of a landmine bar, standing side-on with a staggered stance. Builds the lats and upper back.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.instructions: Throw a medicine ball explosively from your chest to a partner or a wall, like a basketball chest pass. Builds pressing power.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Overhead Throw
exercises.instructions: Throw a medicine ball overhead and backward (or forward against a wall) as explosively as you can, using your whole body.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up with one or both hands on a medicine ball, adding instability and range.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.instructions: Lift a slam ball overhead and throw it down into the floor as hard as you can, then catch it and repeat. Great for power and conditioning.

exercises.name: Mixed Martial Arts
exercises.instructions: Striking and grappling combined: punches, kicks, takedowns and ground work. An intense full-body workout.

exercises.name: Mountain Biking
exercises.instructions: Riding a bike on trails. Builds leg power, endurance and bike handling.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.instructions: From a push-up position, drive your knees toward your chest one at a time in a quick running rhythm, keeping your hips low.

exercises.name: Muay Thai
exercises.instructions: Thai boxing: punches, kicks, elbows and knees. Superb conditioning.

exercises.name: Muscle Clean (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A clean with no squat under the bar: pull the bar and turn your elbows over quickly to catch it standing tall. Builds pulling strength.

exercises.name: Muscle Snatch (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A snatch pulled all the way overhead without dropping under it. Builds pulling strength and overhead positioning.

exercises.name: Muscle-Up
exercises.instructions: An advanced calisthenics move: pull explosively above the bar, rotate your wrists over, and press up into a straight-arm support.

exercises.name: Neck Curl (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back on a bench with your head off the edge and a plate held on your forehead, curl your chin toward your chest. Go slowly and light.

exercises.name: Neck Extension (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Lying face down on a bench with your head off the edge and a plate held on the back of your head, lift your head up. Go slowly and light.

exercises.name: Neck Harness Extension
exercises.instructions: Wearing a neck harness with light weight, lift your head from bent forward to upright. Move slowly with light weight.

exercises.name: Neck Stretch
exercises.instructions: Gently tilt your ear toward your shoulder, using your hand for a light extra stretch. Switch sides and never force it.

exercises.name: Negative Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: Jump or step to the top of a pull-up, then lower yourself as slowly as you can. A great way to build up to full pull-ups.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Bench Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A dumbbell bench press with palms facing each other, which is easier on the shoulders and works the triceps a bit more.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.instructions: A lat pulldown with a palms-facing handle, pulling to your upper chest.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: A pull-up with palms facing each other, often easier on the shoulders and elbows.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
exercises.instructions: A tough hamstring exercise. Kneel with your ankles anchored and lower your straight body toward the floor as slowly as you can, then push back up.

exercises.name: Oblique Crunch
exercises.instructions: A crunch that twists or tilts to bring your ribs toward one hip, for the obliques.

exercises.name: One-Arm Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: The ultimate pulling feat: a full pull-up with one hand.

exercises.name: One-Arm Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up on one hand with your feet wide for balance, keeping your hips square.

exercises.name: Open Water Swim
exercises.instructions: Swimming in lakes, rivers or the sea, where sighting and waves add to the challenge.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Walk with the weight locked out overhead. Builds shoulder stability and core strength; keep your ribs down and biceps by your ears. Carry one dumbbell or two, locked out overhead.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Walk with the weight locked out overhead. Builds shoulder stability and core strength; keep your ribs down and biceps by your ears. Hold the kettlebell with the bell resting on the back of your forearm.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Walk with the weight locked out overhead. Builds shoulder stability and core strength; keep your ribs down and biceps by your ears. Hold a plate overhead by its edges with both hands, arms locked.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Band)
exercises.instructions: The standing press for strong shoulders. Brace your core and glutes, then press the weight from your shoulders to straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to let it pass. The band gets harder as it stretches, so the end of each rep is the toughest.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: The standing press for strong shoulders. Brace your core and glutes, then press the weight from your shoulders to straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to let it pass. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: The standing press for strong shoulders. Brace your core and glutes, then press the weight from your shoulders to straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to let it pass. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: The standing press for strong shoulders. Brace your core and glutes, then press the weight from your shoulders to straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to let it pass. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Overhead Press (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: The standing press for strong shoulders. Brace your core and glutes, then press the weight from your shoulders to straight overhead, moving your head back slightly to let it pass. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Overhead Shrug (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Shrug upward with the bar locked out overhead, for the upper traps and overhead stability.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A squat with a barbell locked out overhead in a wide grip. Demands mobility, stability and control.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (Band)
exercises.instructions: Stretches and builds the triceps. With your upper arms beside your head, lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms. The band gets harder as it stretches, so the end of each rep is the toughest.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Stretches and builds the triceps. With your upper arms beside your head, lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Stretches and builds the triceps. With your upper arms beside your head, lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms. Face away from the stack holding a rope over your head.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Stretches and builds the triceps. With your upper arms beside your head, lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms. Hold one dumbbell by its top end in both hands.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension (EZ Bar)
exercises.instructions: Stretches and builds the triceps. With your upper arms beside your head, lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms. The EZ bar's angled grips are easier on the wrists and elbows.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
exercises.instructions: Raise one arm, bend the elbow to drop your hand behind your head, and gently press the elbow back with your other hand.

exercises.name: Overhead Walking Lunge (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Walking lunges with a weight locked out overhead, for leg strength and core stability.

exercises.name: Padel
exercises.instructions: A racket sport played in a walled court, blending tennis and squash. Fun, social and great for agility.

exercises.name: Pallof Press (Band)
exercises.instructions: An anti-rotation core exercise. Stand side-on to a cable or band, hold the handle at your chest and press it straight out, resisting the pull to twist. Anchor the band at chest height; step farther away to make it harder.

exercises.name: Pallof Press (Cable)
exercises.instructions: An anti-rotation core exercise. Stand side-on to a cable or band, hold the handle at your chest and press it straight out, resisting the pull to twist. Set the pulley at chest height; the farther you stand from the stack, the harder it gets.

exercises.name: Pancake Stretch
exercises.instructions: A seated stretch for the hamstrings and inner thighs. Sit with your legs wide and fold forward from the hips with a long spine.

exercises.name: Pause Squat (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A squat with a two- or three-second pause at the bottom, which builds strength out of the hole and control.

exercises.name: Paused Bench Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A bench press with a clear pause on your chest before pressing, as in competition. Builds control and strength off the chest.

exercises.name: Paused Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A deadlift with a short pause just below the knees, which builds position and strength through the middle of the pull.

exercises.name: Pec Deck (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine fly for the chest. With elbows slightly bent, bring the pads or handles together in front of you, squeeze, and return slowly.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A strict barbell row from the floor with your torso level: row explosively to your lower chest and return the bar to the floor each rep.

exercises.name: Pendulum Squat (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine squat that swings along an arc, keeping your back supported and loading the quads deeply.

exercises.name: Pickleball
exercises.instructions: A paddle sport on a small court with a light plastic ball. Easy to learn and great for agility.

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
exercises.instructions: A deep hip opener. With one shin across the front of your mat and the other leg stretched straight behind, sink your hips and fold forward.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up with your hips high in an upside-down V, which shifts the work to the shoulders. A step toward the handstand push-up.

exercises.name: Pilates
exercises.instructions: Controlled, low-impact exercises focusing on core strength, posture and flexibility.

exercises.name: Pin Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A bench press from safety pins set a few inches above your chest, building strength through the top of the press.

exercises.name: Pin Squat (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A squat from safety pins set at your sticking point, starting each rep from a dead stop.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.instructions: A single-leg squat all the way down with the other leg held straight out in front. Takes strength, balance and mobility.

exercises.name: Planche
exercises.instructions: An advanced calisthenics hold: balance on straight arms with your body horizontal and feet off the floor. Build up through lean and tuck versions.

exercises.name: Planche Lean
exercises.instructions: In a push-up position with straight arms, lean your shoulders forward past your hands. Builds strength toward the planche.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.instructions: A core staple. Hold a straight line from head to heels on your forearms and toes, bracing your abs and squeezing your glutes, without letting your hips sag.

exercises.name: Plank Jack
exercises.instructions: In a plank, jump your feet wide and back together like a jumping jack, keeping your hips level.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
exercises.instructions: In a high plank, tap each shoulder with the opposite hand while keeping your hips still.

exercises.name: Plate Halo
exercises.instructions: Circle a weight plate around your head, holding it by the edges. Builds shoulder mobility and control.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch
exercises.instructions: Pinch two smooth plates together with your fingers and thumb and hold for time. Builds pinch grip.

exercises.name: Plyometric Push-Up
exercises.instructions: An explosive push-up: push hard enough for your hands to leave the floor, then land softly.

exercises.name: Pogo Jump
exercises.instructions: Quick, small bounces on the balls of your feet with stiff ankles, spending as little time on the ground as possible. Builds springy calves.

exercises.name: Power Clean (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A clean from the floor caught in a partial squat above parallel. A classic for explosive power.

exercises.name: Power Jerk (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Dip and drive the bar from your shoulders overhead, catching it in a partial squat with locked arms.

exercises.name: Power Snatch (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A snatch from the floor caught overhead in a partial squat above parallel.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A curl with your upper arms resting on an angled pad, which stops cheating and isolates the biceps. Lower all the way without locking out hard. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (Cable)
exercises.instructions: A curl with your upper arms resting on an angled pad, which stops cheating and isolates the biceps. Lower all the way without locking out hard. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A curl with your upper arms resting on an angled pad, which stops cheating and isolates the biceps. Lower all the way without locking out hard. Dumbbells let you curl one arm at a time.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (EZ Bar)
exercises.instructions: A curl with your upper arms resting on an angled pad, which stops cheating and isolates the biceps. Lower all the way without locking out hard. The EZ bar's angled grips are easier on the wrists and elbows.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A curl with your upper arms resting on an angled pad, which stops cheating and isolates the biceps. Lower all the way without locking out hard. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up with your hands turned out beside your hips and your shoulders leaning forward past them. Builds straight-arm strength toward the planche.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: The king of bodyweight pulls for the back and arms. From a straight-arm hang with an overhand grip, pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower all the way.

exercises.name: Pullover (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Works the lats and chest through a long arc. Lying across or along a bench, lower the weight behind your head with nearly straight arms, then pull it back over your chest. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Pullover (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Works the lats and chest through a long arc. Lying across or along a bench, lower the weight behind your head with nearly straight arms, then pull it back over your chest. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Pullover (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Works the lats and chest through a long arc. Lying across or along a bench, lower the weight behind your head with nearly straight arms, then pull it back over your chest. Hold one dumbbell by its top end in both hands.

exercises.name: Pullover (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Works the lats and chest through a long arc. Lying across or along a bench, lower the weight behind your head with nearly straight arms, then pull it back over your chest. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Push Jerk (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Dip and drive the bar overhead from your shoulders, catching it with a short re-bend of the knees and locked arms.

exercises.name: Push Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press with a quick dip and drive from the legs to help the weight up, letting you handle more than a strict press. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Push Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press with a quick dip and drive from the legs to help the weight up, letting you handle more than a strict press. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your shoulders.

exercises.name: Push Press (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press with a quick dip and drive from the legs to help the weight up, letting you handle more than a strict press. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.instructions: The classic bodyweight press for the chest, shoulders and triceps. With hands under your shoulders and body straight, lower your chest to the floor, then push back up.

exercises.name: Rack Pull (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A partial deadlift from pins or blocks around knee height, which overloads the top of the pull and the upper back. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Rack Pull (Trap Bar)
exercises.instructions: A partial deadlift from pins or blocks around knee height, which overloads the top of the pull and the upper back. The trap bar keeps the load in line with your body, which is easier on the lower back.

exercises.name: Racquetball
exercises.instructions: A fast indoor racket sport played off every wall of the court. Great for agility and conditioning.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly (Band)
exercises.instructions: Works the rear shoulders and upper back. Bent over or facing a pad, raise your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in the elbows, squeezing your shoulder blades. The band gets harder as it stretches, so the end of each rep is the toughest.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Works the rear shoulders and upper back. Bent over or facing a pad, raise your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in the elbows, squeezing your shoulder blades. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Works the rear shoulders and upper back. Bent over or facing a pad, raise your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in the elbows, squeezing your shoulder blades. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Works the rear shoulders and upper back. Bent over or facing a pad, raise your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in the elbows, squeezing your shoulder blades. Sit facing the pad of a reverse pec deck.

exercises.name: Recumbent Bike
exercises.instructions: A reclined stationary bike with back support. Low-impact cardio that's easy on the back and joints.

exercises.name: Renegade Row (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: In a push-up position holding dumbbells, row one dumbbell to your hip while the other arm and your core hold you steady.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back with knees bent, curl your hips off the floor toward your ribs, then lower slowly.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A curl with an overhand grip, palms down, which works the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl (Cable)
exercises.instructions: A curl with an overhand grip, palms down, which works the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A curl with an overhand grip, palms down, which works the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl (EZ Bar)
exercises.instructions: A curl with an overhand grip, palms down, which works the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps. The EZ bar's angled grips are easier on the wrists and elbows.

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Lying face down on a reverse hyper bench, swing your straight legs up behind you, squeezing the glutes, then lower under control.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.instructions: Step backward into a lunge, lower until both knees reach about 90°, then drive back up through your front heel. Easier on the knees than a forward lunge.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Step backward into a lunge, lower until both knees reach about 90°, then drive back up through your front heel. Easier on the knees than a forward lunge. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Step backward into a lunge, lower until both knees reach about 90°, then drive back up through your front heel. Easier on the knees than a forward lunge. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, which keeps the weight low and easy to balance.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Step backward into a lunge, lower until both knees reach about 90°, then drive back up through your front heel. Easier on the knees than a forward lunge. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides, or one at your chest, goblet-style.

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic
exercises.instructions: Kneel upright with your body straight, then lean back from the knees as far as you can control and return. Stretches and strengthens the quads.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: With your forearms resting on your thighs, palms down, lift the weight with your wrists. Builds the backs of the forearms. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: With your forearms resting on your thighs, palms down, lift the weight with your wrists. Builds the backs of the forearms. Dumbbells let you work one wrist at a time.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Bench Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A bench press with an underhand grip, which brings in more upper chest and triceps. Use a spotter. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Bench Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A bench press with an underhand grip, which brings in more upper chest and triceps. Use a spotter. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.instructions: A lat pulldown with an underhand, shoulder-width grip, bringing in more biceps.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Triceps Pushdown
exercises.instructions: A triceps pushdown with an underhand grip, palms up.

exercises.name: Ring Dip
exercises.instructions: A dip on gymnastic rings. The rings wobble, so your shoulders and core work much harder than on bars.

exercises.name: Ring Muscle-Up
exercises.instructions: A muscle-up on rings: pull, turn over into a deep dip with a false grip, then press up to support.

exercises.name: Ring Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up with your hands in low rings, which adds instability and a deeper stretch.

exercises.name: Ring Row
exercises.instructions: A row hanging under a pair of rings, body straight. Walk your feet forward to make it harder.

exercises.name: Ring Support Hold
exercises.instructions: Hold yourself above a pair of rings on straight arms, turning the rings out slightly. The foundation of ring training.

exercises.name: RKC Plank
exercises.instructions: An all-out plank: squeeze everything, drive your elbows toward your toes and your glutes tight. Hold for short, intense bursts.

exercises.name: Rock Climbing
exercises.instructions: Climbing rock walls, indoors or out, with ropes. Builds grip, pulling strength and endurance.

exercises.name: Rolling Triceps Extension (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A dumbbell triceps extension on a bench that rolls the weights back behind your head, then presses them up. Easy on the elbows.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A hip hinge for the hamstrings and glutes. With knees softly bent, push your hips back and lower the weight along your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand tall. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A hip hinge for the hamstrings and glutes. With knees softly bent, push your hips back and lower the weight along your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand tall. Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs and keep them close to your legs as you hinge.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A hip hinge for the hamstrings and glutes. With knees softly bent, push your hips back and lower the weight along your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand tall. Hold the kettlebell in both hands, or one in each hand, close to your legs.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: A hip hinge for the hamstrings and glutes. With knees softly bent, push your hips back and lower the weight along your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand tall. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (Trap Bar)
exercises.instructions: A hip hinge for the hamstrings and glutes. With knees softly bent, push your hips back and lower the weight along your legs until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand tall. The trap bar keeps the load in line with your body, which is easier on the lower back.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.instructions: Climb a rope using your arms and a foot lock with your legs. Builds grip and pulling strength.

exercises.name: Rotary Torso (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A seated rotation machine for the obliques: turn your torso against resistance, slowly and under control.

exercises.name: Rotational Medicine Ball Throw
exercises.instructions: Stand side-on to a wall and throw a medicine ball explosively into it by rotating through your hips and torso. Builds rotational power.

exercises.name: Rowing (On Water)
exercises.instructions: Rowing a boat on water, a full-body endurance sport powered mostly by the legs and back.

exercises.name: Rowing Machine
exercises.instructions: Full-body cardio on an indoor rower. Push with your legs, then swing your body back and pull the handle to your ribs; reverse the order on the way back.

exercises.name: Rucking
exercises.instructions: Walking with a weighted backpack. Builds endurance, the legs and posture with low impact.

exercises.name: Rugby
exercises.instructions: A full-contact team sport of running, tackling and scrummaging.

exercises.name: Running
exercises.instructions: The simplest cardio there is. Builds endurance, heart health and leg strength.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.instructions: Sit leaning back with your feet off the floor and twist your torso side to side, bringing your hands to the floor beside each hip. Works the obliques.

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Sit leaning back with your feet off the floor and twist your torso side to side, bringing your hands to the floor beside each hip. Works the obliques. Hold one dumbbell by its ends at your chest.

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Medicine Ball)
exercises.instructions: Sit leaning back with your feet off the floor and twist your torso side to side, bringing your hands to the floor beside each hip. Works the obliques. Hold the ball at your chest and touch it to the floor beside each hip.

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Sit leaning back with your feet off the floor and twist your torso side to side, bringing your hands to the floor beside each hip. Works the obliques. Hold a weight plate firmly by its edges.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
exercises.instructions: A back squat with a padded, cambered safety squat bar that's easier on the shoulders and works the upper back hard.

exercises.name: Sandbag Carry
exercises.instructions: Carry a heavy sandbag, bear-hugged or on your shoulder, as far as you can.

exercises.name: Sandbag Clean
exercises.instructions: Lift a sandbag from the floor to your chest in one explosive hip drive, catching it on your forearms.

exercises.name: Sandbag Over Shoulder
exercises.instructions: Pick up a heavy sandbag and toss it over one shoulder, alternating sides. Explosive full-body power.

exercises.name: Sauna
exercises.instructions: Heat exposure for relaxation and recovery. Stay hydrated and leave if you feel dizzy.

exercises.name: Scaption (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A raise in the scapular plane: lift your arms at about 30° in front of your sides with thumbs up, to shoulder height. Friendly on the shoulders.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: From a dead hang, pull your shoulder blades down and back to lift your body slightly without bending your arms. Builds shoulder control for pull-ups.

exercises.name: Scissor Kick
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back with legs raised, cross them over each other in a quick scissoring motion.

exercises.name: Scorpion Stretch
exercises.instructions: Lying face down with arms out, swing one foot over toward the opposite hand to stretch the hips and lower back.

exercises.name: Seal Row (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A row lying face down on a raised bench, pulling the weight from below. Takes the lower back and momentum out of the row entirely. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Seal Row (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A row lying face down on a raised bench, pulling the weight from below. Takes the lower back and momentum out of the row entirely. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Seated Bicep Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A dumbbell curl done seated, which limits body swing.

exercises.name: Seated Box Jump
exercises.instructions: Sit on a bench, then jump onto a box from the seated position. Removes the countermovement to build pure starting power.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.instructions: A classic back builder. Sitting with your chest up, pull the handle to your lower ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and return slowly.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A calf raise with knees bent and the load on your thighs, which targets the soleus. Rest the barbell on a pad across your thighs, just above the knees.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A calf raise with knees bent and the load on your thighs, which targets the soleus. Rest the dumbbells on your knees.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A calf raise with knees bent and the load on your thighs, which targets the soleus. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Seated Dip (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A dip machine: press the handles down until your arms are straight, working the triceps and chest.

exercises.name: Seated Good Morning (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A good morning done seated on a bench: hinge forward with a flat back and return. Targets the lower back.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
exercises.instructions: Sit with one or both legs straight and fold forward from your hips toward your toes, keeping your back long.

exercises.name: Seated Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A lateral raise done seated, which removes leg drive and swing.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine leg curl done seated: curl the pad down and back toward your seat, squeeze, and return slowly.

exercises.name: Seated Overhead Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press seated on an upright bench, which limits leg drive and back arch. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Seated Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press seated on an upright bench, which limits leg drive and back arch. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Seated Row (Band)
exercises.instructions: A seated row for the upper back: pull the handles to your ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and return slowly. Sit with your legs straight and loop the band around your feet.

exercises.name: Seated Row (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A seated row for the upper back: pull the handles to your ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and return slowly. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing
exercises.instructions: Throwing punch combinations and moving your feet without a partner or bag. Great cardio and technique work.

exercises.name: Shoulder Dislocate
exercises.instructions: A shoulder mobility drill. Hold a band or stick with a wide grip and pass it from in front of you over your head to behind your back with straight arms.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press (Cable)
exercises.instructions: A seated press for the shoulders on a machine or cable: press the handles overhead until your arms are straight, then lower slowly. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A seated press for the shoulders on a machine or cable: press the handles overhead until your arms are straight, then lower slowly. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Shoulder to Overhead (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Get the bar from your shoulders to overhead any way you like: press, push press or jerk.

exercises.name: Shrimp Squat
exercises.instructions: A single-leg squat holding your rear foot behind you, lowering until your back knee touches the floor.

exercises.name: Shrug (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Shrug (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Shrug (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.

exercises.name: Shrug (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Shrug (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Shrug (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Shrug (Trap Bar)
exercises.instructions: Builds the upper traps. Stand tall holding the weight, lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, and lower slowly without rolling them. The trap bar keeps the load in line with your body, which is easier on the lower back.

exercises.name: Shuttle Run
exercises.instructions: Sprint back and forth between two lines, turning quickly at each end. Builds speed and agility.

exercises.name: Side Bend (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Holding a weight in one hand, bend sideways toward it, then use your obliques to pull yourself back upright. Stand side-on to a low pulley, holding the handle.

exercises.name: Side Bend (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Holding a weight in one hand, bend sideways toward it, then use your obliques to pull yourself back upright. Keep the dumbbell close to your leg as you bend.

exercises.name: Side Bend (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Holding a weight in one hand, bend sideways toward it, then use your obliques to pull yourself back upright. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Side Bend (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Holding a weight in one hand, bend sideways toward it, then use your obliques to pull yourself back upright. Hold a weight plate firmly by its edges.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.instructions: Hold your body in a straight line on one forearm and the side of your foot. Works the obliques and the side of the hips.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
exercises.instructions: Lying on your side with legs straight, lift the top leg toward the ceiling and lower it slowly. Targets the side glutes.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Bench Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A dumbbell bench press one arm at a time, which makes your core work to keep you on the bench.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press
exercises.instructions: A standing one-arm cable press, which trains the chest and resists rotation through the core.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Fly
exercises.instructions: A one-arm cable fly across your body, for a strong squeeze on each side of the chest.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
exercises.instructions: A kettlebell swing with one hand, which adds a rotational and grip challenge.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.instructions: A one-arm cable pulldown for a stronger stretch and contraction in each lat.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press one arm at a time, which challenges your core to stay upright. Press with your palm facing in or forward, whichever feels better on your shoulder.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Overhead Press (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press one arm at a time, which challenges your core to stay upright. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Overhead Triceps Extension (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm dumbbell triceps extension behind your head.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Row (Band)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm row for the lats and upper back. Row the weight toward your hip, keeping your torso still, then lower it for a full stretch. The band gets harder as it stretches, so the end of each rep is the toughest.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Row (Cable)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm row for the lats and upper back. Row the weight toward your hip, keeping your torso still, then lower it for a full stretch. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Row (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm row for the lats and upper back. Row the weight toward your hip, keeping your torso still, then lower it for a full stretch. Brace your free hand and knee on a bench for support.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Row (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A one-arm row for the lats and upper back. Row the weight toward your hip, keeping your torso still, then lower it for a full stretch. A kettlebell's offset weight adds a grip and stability challenge.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Row
exercises.instructions: A seated cable row one arm at a time, for a longer stretch and pull on each side.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Triceps Pushdown
exercises.instructions: A one-arm cable pushdown for the triceps.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Box Jump
exercises.instructions: Jump onto a box from one leg and land on both, or on the same leg. Builds single-leg power.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: A calf raise on one leg, ideally on a step so your heel can drop below it. Rise fully onto the ball of your foot and lower slowly.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A calf raise on one leg, ideally on a step so your heel can drop below it. Rise fully onto the ball of your foot and lower slowly. Hold a dumbbell in the hand on the working side.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.instructions: A glute bridge on one leg with the other extended. Lift your hips until level without letting them tilt.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
exercises.instructions: A hip thrust on one leg with the other lifted, for more glute work per side. Keep your hips level as you drive up.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A hip thrust on one leg with the other lifted, for more glute work per side. Keep your hips level as you drive up. Rest a dumbbell on the working hip and hold it in place.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop
exercises.instructions: Hop forward or in place on one leg, landing softly and springing straight back up. Builds ankle stiffness and single-leg power.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Extension (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A leg extension one leg at a time, to balance strength between your quads.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Press (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A leg press with one foot centered on the platform, to train each leg on its own.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
exercises.instructions: A one-leg hip hinge for the hamstrings, glutes and balance. Stand on one leg, hinge forward as the other leg reaches straight back until your body is nearly level, then stand tall.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A one-leg hip hinge for the hamstrings, glutes and balance. Stand on one leg, hinge forward as the other leg reaches straight back until your body is nearly level, then stand tall. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A one-leg hip hinge for the hamstrings, glutes and balance. Stand on one leg, hinge forward as the other leg reaches straight back until your body is nearly level, then stand tall. Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite your standing leg, or one in each hand.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A one-leg hip hinge for the hamstrings, glutes and balance. Stand on one leg, hinge forward as the other leg reaches straight back until your body is nearly level, then stand tall. Hold the kettlebell in the hand opposite your standing leg.

exercises.name: Single-Under
exercises.instructions: Basic jump rope: one turn of the rope for each small, light jump.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat
exercises.instructions: A quad exercise where you lean back and let your knees travel far forward as you lower, keeping your hips extended. Hold onto something for balance.

exercises.name: Sit-Up
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet anchored, then curl all the way up until your chest is near your thighs, and lower slowly.

exercises.name: Skateboarding
exercises.instructions: Riding a skateboard: balance, leg strength and coordination.

exercises.name: Skater Jump
exercises.instructions: Bound sideways from one leg to the other like a speed skater, landing softly and balancing briefly each time.

exercises.name: Ski Erg
exercises.instructions: A standing cardio machine that mimics cross-country skiing: pull the handles down by hinging at the hips and driving with your arms.

exercises.name: Skin the Cat
exercises.instructions: From a hang on rings or a bar, tuck your knees and rotate backward through your arms until your feet point to the floor, then reverse. Builds shoulder mobility.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A lying triceps extension. With your upper arms vertical, bend your elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead, then straighten your arms. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A lying triceps extension. With your upper arms vertical, bend your elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead, then straighten your arms. Dumbbells let your wrists turn freely, which is easier on the elbows.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher (EZ Bar)
exercises.instructions: A lying triceps extension. With your upper arms vertical, bend your elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead, then straighten your arms. The EZ bar's angled grips are easier on the wrists and elbows.

exercises.name: Sled Drag
exercises.instructions: Pull a loaded sled with a harness or handles while walking forward. Builds the legs and conditioning with little stress on the joints.

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.instructions: Drive a loaded sled forward with a strong forward lean and short, powerful steps. Brutal conditioning for the legs.

exercises.name: Sled Rope Pull
exercises.instructions: Pull a sled toward you hand over hand with a rope, standing or seated. Works the back, arms and grip.

exercises.name: Sledgehammer Strike
exercises.instructions: Swing a sledgehammer onto a tire, sliding your hands along the handle, switching sides. Builds power and conditioning.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.instructions: Lying on your side with your bottom arm bent 90° in front, gently press that forearm toward the floor to stretch the back of the shoulder.

exercises.name: Slider Leg Curl
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back with your heels on sliders, lift your hips and slide your heels in toward your glutes, then out again. Tough on the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Snatch (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: An Olympic lift that takes the weight from the floor to overhead in one explosive motion, caught with straight arms in a squat. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Snatch (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: An Olympic lift that takes the weight from the floor to overhead in one explosive motion, caught with straight arms in a squat. Usually done one arm at a time, pulling the dumbbell from between your feet to overhead.

exercises.name: Snatch (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: An Olympic lift that takes the weight from the floor to overhead in one explosive motion, caught with straight arms in a squat. One arm at a time: swing the kettlebell back, drive your hips so it floats up, and punch through to lock it out overhead.

exercises.name: Snatch Balance (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: From the bar on your back in a snatch grip, drive down quickly under it into an overhead squat. Builds speed and confidence under the bar.

exercises.name: Snatch Pull (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: The first part of a snatch with a wide grip: pull from the floor and extend explosively with a shrug, without dropping under the bar.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A deadlift with a wide snatch grip, which lengthens the pull and works the upper back and traps more.

exercises.name: Snowboarding
exercises.instructions: Riding down snowy slopes on a board. Builds leg strength and balance.

exercises.name: Snowshoeing
exercises.instructions: Hiking through snow on snowshoes. Tough, low-impact cardio.

exercises.name: Soccer
exercises.instructions: The world's game: continuous running, sprints and quick direction changes.

exercises.name: Softball
exercises.instructions: A bat-and-ball sport like baseball with a larger ball, underhand pitching and short sprints.

exercises.name: Sots Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: An overhead press from the bottom of a front squat, with the bar pressed from behind your neck. Demands mobility and control; keep it light.

exercises.name: Spanish Squat (Band)
exercises.instructions: A quad-focused squat with a heavy band behind your knees anchored in front of you, letting you sit back with vertical shins. Kind to sore knees.

exercises.name: Spider Curl (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A curl lying face down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, for a hard squeeze at the top. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Spider Curl (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A curl lying face down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, for a hard squeeze at the top. Dumbbells work each side on its own and allow a freer, more natural path.

exercises.name: Spider Curl (EZ Bar)
exercises.instructions: A curl lying face down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down, for a hard squeeze at the top. The EZ bar's angled grips are easier on the wrists and elbows.

exercises.name: Spiderman Lunge with Rotation
exercises.instructions: A dynamic stretch: step into a deep lunge, put the same-side hand down inside your foot, then rotate your other arm up to the sky.

exercises.name: Spiderman Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up where you bring one knee to the same-side elbow as you lower, alternating sides.

exercises.name: Spin Bike
exercises.instructions: An indoor cycling bike with a heavy flywheel, for steady rides or hard interval classes.

exercises.name: Split Jerk (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Dip and drive the bar overhead, splitting your feet into a lunge to catch it with locked arms, then bring your feet together.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.instructions: A lunge with both feet planted. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through your front foot.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A lunge with both feet planted. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through your front foot. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A lunge with both feet planted. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through your front foot. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, which keeps the weight low and easy to balance.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A lunge with both feet planted. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through your front foot. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides, or one at your chest, goblet-style.

exercises.name: Split Squat (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: A lunge with both feet planted. Lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive up through your front foot. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Spoto Press (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A bench press that pauses an inch above your chest without touching it, building control and strength at the bottom.

exercises.name: Sprawl
exercises.instructions: A burpee without the push-up or jump: drop your hips to the floor, kicking your feet back, then pop back up. Used in combat sports.

exercises.name: Sprint
exercises.instructions: Running all-out for a short distance. Builds speed and power.

exercises.name: Squash
exercises.instructions: A fast racket sport played off the walls of an enclosed court. Superb agility and conditioning.

exercises.name: Squat (Band)
exercises.instructions: The king of leg exercises for the quads, glutes and core. With feet about shoulder-width apart, sit your hips back and down until your thighs are at least level with the floor, then drive up, chest up. Stand on the band with it looped over your shoulders; it gets harder as you stand up.

exercises.name: Squat (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: The king of leg exercises for the quads, glutes and core. With feet about shoulder-width apart, sit your hips back and down until your thighs are at least level with the floor, then drive up, chest up. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Squat (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: The king of leg exercises for the quads, glutes and core. With feet about shoulder-width apart, sit your hips back and down until your thighs are at least level with the floor, then drive up, chest up. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides or on your shoulders.

exercises.name: Squat (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: The king of leg exercises for the quads, glutes and core. With feet about shoulder-width apart, sit your hips back and down until your thighs are at least level with the floor, then drive up, chest up. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Squeeze Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A dumbbell press with the dumbbells squeezed together the whole time, which keeps constant tension on the inner chest.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Crunch
exercises.instructions: A crunch with your lower back on a stability ball, which adds range. Curl your ribs toward your hips and return.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back with your heels on a ball, lift your hips and roll the ball in toward your glutes, then out.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up with your hands or feet on a stability ball, adding balance and core demand.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Rollout
exercises.instructions: Kneeling with your forearms on a stability ball, roll it forward as far as you can without your back sagging, then pull it back.

exercises.name: Stair Climber
exercises.instructions: A machine that climbs a revolving staircase. Hard, low-impact cardio for the legs and glutes.

exercises.name: Stair Running
exercises.instructions: Running up flights of stairs and walking down. Builds leg power and conditioning.

exercises.name: Stand-Up Paddleboarding
exercises.instructions: Paddling while standing on a board. Works balance, the core and the upper body.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: Builds the calves. Standing with the balls of your feet on a step, rise onto your toes as high as you can, pause, then lower your heels below the step for a full stretch.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the calves. Standing with the balls of your feet on a step, rise onto your toes as high as you can, pause, then lower your heels below the step for a full stretch. Hold the bar across your upper back, as for a squat.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the calves. Standing with the balls of your feet on a step, rise onto your toes as high as you can, pause, then lower your heels below the step for a full stretch. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
exercises.instructions: Builds the calves. Standing with the balls of your feet on a step, rise onto your toes as high as you can, pause, then lower your heels below the step for a full stretch. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (Smith Machine)
exercises.instructions: Builds the calves. Standing with the balls of your feet on a step, rise onto your toes as high as you can, pause, then lower your heels below the step for a full stretch. The Smith machine fixes the bar's path for extra stability; set the safety stops before you start.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
exercises.instructions: Lean into a wall with one leg back and its heel pressed into the floor to stretch the calf. Bend the back knee a little to stretch deeper.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold
exercises.instructions: Stand tall, then fold forward from your hips and let your upper body hang toward the floor, knees softly bent. Stretches the hamstrings and back.

exercises.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
exercises.instructions: Rest one heel on a low step with the leg straight and hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch behind the thigh.

exercises.name: Standing Leg Curl (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine leg curl one leg at a time while standing.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
exercises.instructions: Stand on one leg and pull your other heel toward your glutes, knees together, to stretch the front of the thigh. Hold onto something for balance.

exercises.name: Star Jump
exercises.instructions: An explosive jump spreading your arms and legs out wide into a star shape in the air, landing softly.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.instructions: Indoor cycling on an upright stationary bike. Easy on the joints and simple to pace.

exercises.name: Step Aerobics
exercises.instructions: Rhythmic cardio stepping on and off a low platform to music.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.instructions: Builds the legs one at a time. Step onto a box or bench with one foot and drive through that heel to stand up tall, then step down with control.

exercises.name: Step-Up (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the legs one at a time. Step onto a box or bench with one foot and drive through that heel to stand up tall, then step down with control. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Step-Up (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the legs one at a time. Step onto a box or bench with one foot and drive through that heel to stand up tall, then step down with control. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, which keeps the weight low and easy to balance.

exercises.name: Step-Up (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Builds the legs one at a time. Step onto a box or bench with one foot and drive through that heel to stand up tall, then step down with control. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides, or one at your chest, goblet-style.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A deadlift with nearly straight legs, hinging at the hips to stretch and work the hamstrings. Each rep often starts from the floor. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A deadlift with nearly straight legs, hinging at the hips to stretch and work the hamstrings. Each rep often starts from the floor. Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs and keep them close to your legs.

exercises.name: Stir the Pot
exercises.instructions: In a forearm plank on a stability ball, draw small circles with your forearms, stirring the ball, while keeping your body still.

exercises.name: Stone to Shoulder
exercises.instructions: A strongman lift: pick up an atlas stone and hoist it onto one shoulder.

exercises.name: Straight Bar Dip
exercises.instructions: A dip on a single straight bar in front of your body. A key step toward the muscle-up.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown (Band)
exercises.instructions: An isolation exercise for the lats. With straight arms, pull the bar or band from overhead down to your thighs in an arc, then return slowly. Anchor the band high overhead.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown (Cable)
exercises.instructions: An isolation exercise for the lats. With straight arms, pull the bar or band from overhead down to your thighs in an arc, then return slowly. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Stretching
exercises.instructions: General stretching and flexibility work to loosen tight muscles and improve range of motion.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Walk holding a heavy weight in one hand only, like a suitcase. Your core works hard to keep you upright; switch sides. Hold the dumbbell by the middle of the handle so it stays level.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: Walk holding a heavy weight in one hand only, like a suitcase. Your core works hard to keep you upright; switch sides. The kettlebell hangs close to your leg, which is comfortable for long carries.

exercises.name: Suitcase Deadlift (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A deadlift with one weight held at your side, which trains your core to resist leaning. Hold the dumbbell by the middle of the handle so it stays level.

exercises.name: Suitcase Deadlift (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A deadlift with one weight held at your side, which trains your core to resist leaning. The kettlebell sits close to your leg, so it's easy to keep in line.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A wide-stance deadlift with your hands inside your knees, which uses more glutes and inner thighs and keeps your torso upright. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A wide-stance deadlift with your hands inside your knees, which uses more glutes and inner thighs and keeps your torso upright. Hold one heavy dumbbell by its end, hanging between your legs.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A wide-stance deadlift with your hands inside your knees, which uses more glutes and inner thighs and keeps your torso upright. Hold one heavy kettlebell by the handle, hanging between your legs.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift High Pull (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: From a wide sumo stance, pull the weight explosively from the floor up to your chin with elbows high. A conditioning staple. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift High Pull (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: From a wide sumo stance, pull the weight explosively from the floor up to your chin with elbows high. A conditioning staple. Grip the kettlebell with both hands and pull it to your chin.

exercises.name: Sun Salutation
exercises.instructions: A flowing yoga sequence moving through forward folds, plank, cobra and downward dog with your breath.

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.instructions: Lie face down and lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor together, squeezing your back and glutes, then lower.

exercises.name: Superman Hold
exercises.instructions: Hold the lifted superman position, arms and legs off the floor, for time.

exercises.name: Supine Spinal Twist
exercises.instructions: Lying on your back, drop your bent knees to one side while your shoulders stay down, to gently twist and relax the spine.

exercises.name: Surfing
exercises.instructions: Paddling out and riding waves. Works the shoulders, core and balance.

exercises.name: Suspension Bicep Curl
exercises.instructions: Lean back holding the straps with palms up, then curl your hands toward your forehead, pulling your body up.

exercises.name: Suspension Push-Up
exercises.instructions: A push-up with your hands or feet in suspension straps, which adds instability for the chest and core.

exercises.name: Suspension Row
exercises.instructions: Lean back holding the straps with your body straight, then row your chest up to your hands. Walk your feet forward to make it harder.

exercises.name: Suspension Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: Lean forward holding the straps with your arms straight, bend your elbows to lower your head between your hands, then press back out.

exercises.name: Svend Press (Plate)
exercises.instructions: Squeeze two plates together between your palms at your chest and press them straight out and back. Works the inner chest.

exercises.name: Swimming
exercises.instructions: Laps in the pool: full-body, low-impact cardio.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row (Landmine)
exercises.instructions: A heavy row pulling a landmine or T-bar handle toward your chest, torso hinged forward with a flat back. Builds a thick upper back. Straddle the bar and pull with a V-handle just under the sleeve.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A heavy row pulling a landmine or T-bar handle toward your chest, torso hinged forward with a flat back. Builds a thick upper back. The machine guides the movement, so you can focus on the working muscle.

exercises.name: Table Tennis
exercises.instructions: Ping-pong: fast reactions, footwork and coordination.

exercises.name: Taekwondo
exercises.instructions: A Korean martial art known for fast, high kicks. Builds flexibility, speed and power.

exercises.name: Tai Chi
exercises.instructions: Slow, flowing martial-arts movements for balance, mobility and calm.

exercises.name: Tate Press (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A dumbbell triceps press lying on a bench, bringing the dumbbells down toward your chest with elbows out, then pressing up.

exercises.name: Tennis
exercises.instructions: A racket sport of sprints, lunges and powerful strokes.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation
exercises.instructions: A mobility drill for the upper back: from hands and knees or lying on your side, rotate your upper body open, reaching one arm up and back.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.instructions: On hands and knees, reach one arm under your body toward the other side, lowering that shoulder to the floor to stretch the upper back.

exercises.name: Thruster (Barbell)
exercises.instructions: A front squat straight into an overhead press in one fluid move, using the drive from the squat to press. A conditioning classic. A barbell lets you move the most weight.

exercises.name: Thruster (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: A front squat straight into an overhead press in one fluid move, using the drive from the squat to press. A conditioning classic. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your shoulders.

exercises.name: Thruster (Kettlebell)
exercises.instructions: A front squat straight into an overhead press in one fluid move, using the drive from the squat to press. A conditioning classic. Hold the kettlebells in the rack position, resting on your forearms.

exercises.name: Tibialis Raise
exercises.instructions: Lean back against a wall with your heels out in front, then lift your toes toward your shins. Builds the front of the lower legs and helps the knees.

exercises.name: Tire Flip
exercises.instructions: A strongman staple: squat down, drive a heavy tire up from its edge with your legs and hips, then push it over.

exercises.name: Toe Touch
exercises.instructions: A crunch variation lying on your back with legs straight up, reaching your hands toward your toes.

exercises.name: Toes-to-Bar
exercises.instructions: Hanging from a bar, raise your feet all the way up to touch the bar between your hands.

exercises.name: Trail Running
exercises.instructions: Running on off-road trails, where hills and uneven ground build strength and agility.

exercises.name: Treadmill Run
exercises.instructions: Running on a treadmill, with easy control over pace and incline.

exercises.name: Treadmill Walk
exercises.instructions: Walking on a treadmill: gentle, steady cardio.

exercises.name: Triceps Dip
exercises.instructions: A dip with an upright torso to focus on the triceps. On parallel bars, lower until your elbows reach about 90°, then press up.

exercises.name: Triceps Extension (Machine)
exercises.instructions: A machine triceps extension: straighten your arms against resistance, then return slowly.

exercises.name: Triceps Kickback (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Hinge forward with your upper arm pinned by your side, then straighten your elbow to push the weight back. Squeeze at full extension. The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.

exercises.name: Triceps Kickback (Dumbbell)
exercises.instructions: Hinge forward with your upper arm pinned by your side, then straighten your elbow to push the weight back. Squeeze at full extension. Work one arm at a time braced on a bench, or both together while bent over.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Band)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the triceps. With your elbows pinned to your sides, push the bar or band down until your arms are straight, then let it rise slowly. Anchor the band high overhead.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Cable)
exercises.instructions: Isolates the triceps. With your elbows pinned to your sides, push the bar or band down until your arms are straight, then let it rise slowly. Use a straight bar, V-bar or rope.

exercises.name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
exercises.instructions: A cable pushdown with a rope, spreading the ends apart at the bottom for a hard triceps squeeze.

exercises.name: Truck Pull
exercises.instructions: A strongman event: pull a truck with a harness and rope, driving with short, powerful steps.

exercises.name: Tuck Front Lever
exercises.instructions: A front lever with your knees tucked to your chest, back level with the floor. The first step toward the full front lever.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
exercises.instructions: Jump straight up and pull your knees to your chest at the top, landing softly.

exercises.name: Tuck Planche
